original.target_description: Study 1, European and Asian Americans, mortality-salience versus dental-pain primes; PAS attitudes and bail assignment. Exact target test/outcome/subgroup unresolved.

notes: All three rows supply identical broad Study 1 descriptions and p.3 locators. They do not distinguish PAS versus bail, omnibus interaction versus simple contrast, or subgroup. Assigning a candidate to a row would require unsupported row-order or numeric matching. Candidate tests, printed p.1021 (PDF p.3): Condition × ethnicity interaction, multivariate PAS/bail: F(2, 37) = 5.31, p = .009.; Condition × ethnicity interaction, PAS: F(1, 38) = 10.263, p = .003; Condition × ethnicity interaction, bail: F(1, 38) = 3.036, p = .090.; Mortality salience versus control, European American PAS: t(20)= 2.10, p = .048; Mortality salience versus control, Asian American PAS: t(18) = 2.73, p = .013; Mortality salience versus control, European American bail: t(20) = 1.89, p = .072.; Mortality salience versus control, Asian American bail: t(18) < 1, p = .472.; Ethnicity main effect, multivariate PAS/bail: F(2, 37) = 3.13, p = .055; Ethnicity main effect, PAS: F(1, ... 38) = 5.02, p = .031.; Ethnicity main effect, bail: F(1, 38) = 3.30, p = ... .077.; European versus Asian American PAS, control: t(16) = 5.17, p < ... .001; European versus Asian American PAS, mortality salience: t(22) < 1, p = .53.; European versus Asian American bail, control: t(16) = 2.70, ... p = .015; European versus Asian American bail, mortality salience: t(22) < 1, p = .95.. All statistics and same-test p values retained as candidates only; F and t metrics and printed bounds preserved. Study 1 Participants, printed p.1020 (PDF p.2), reports 22 European American and 20 Asian American participants. Candidate full-study participant count only: 22 + 20 = 42. Ethnic groups are mutually exclusive, but a row-specific critical test and final analytic sample are not established. This candidate is not promoted to analytic N; subgroup counts remain distinct. No N inferred from degrees of freedom. Exclusions are not stated in Study 1 Participants/Results. PDF pages 2–3 visually inspected. Appended corrigendum corrects Study 2 N and states that reported standard deviations in both studies are standard errors of estimated marginal means. No metric conversions performed. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
